31 module clint_apb import cvw::*;  #(parameter cvw_t P) (
32   input  logic                PCLK, PRESETn,
33   input  logic                PSEL,
34   input  logic [15:0]         PADDR,
35   input  logic [P.XLEN-1:0]   PWDATA,
36   input  logic [P.XLEN/8-1:0] PSTRB,
37   input  logic                PWRITE,
38   input  logic                PENABLE,
39   output logic [P.XLEN-1:0]   PRDATA,
40   output logic                PREADY,
41   output logic [63:0] MTIME,
42   output logic                MTimerInt, MSwInt
43 );
44 
45   // register map
46   localparam CLINT_MSIP     = 16'h0000;
47   localparam CLINT_MTIMECMP = 16'h4000;
48   localparam CLINT_MTIME    = 16'hBFF8;
49 
50   logic                       MSIP;
51   logic [15:0]                entry;
52   logic                       memwrite;
53   logic [63:0] MTIMECMP;
54   integer                     i, j;
55 
56   assign memwrite = PWRITE & PENABLE & PSEL;  // only write in access phase
57   assign PREADY   = 1'b1;                     // CLINT never takes >1 cycle to respond
58 
59   // word aligned reads
60   if (P.XLEN==64) assign entry = {PADDR[15:3], 3'b000};
61   else            assign entry = {PADDR[15:2], 2'b00};
62 
63   // DH 2/20/21: Eventually allow MTIME to run off a separate clock
64   // This will require synchronizing MTIME to the system clock
65   // before it is read or compared to MTIMECMP.
66   // It will also require synchronizing the write to MTIMECMP.
67   // Use req and ack signals synchronized across the clock domains.
68 
69   // register access
70   if (P.XLEN==64) begin:clint // 64-bit
71     always_ff @(posedge PCLK) begin
72       case(entry)
73         CLINT_MSIP:     PRDATA <= {63'b0, MSIP};
74         CLINT_MTIMECMP: PRDATA <= MTIMECMP;
75         CLINT_MTIME:    PRDATA <= MTIME;
76         default:        PRDATA <= '0;
77       endcase
78     end
79     always_ff @(posedge PCLK)
80       if (~PRESETn) begin
81         MSIP <= 1'b0;
82         MTIMECMP <= 64'hFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF; // Spec says MTIMECMP is not reset, but we reset to maximum value to prevent spurious timer interrupts
83       end else if (memwrite) begin
84         if (entry == CLINT_MSIP) MSIP <= PWDATA[0];
85         if (entry == CLINT_MTIMECMP) begin
86           for(i=0;i<P.XLEN/8;i++)
87             if(PSTRB[i])
88               MTIMECMP[i*8 +: 8] <= PWDATA[i*8 +: 8];
89         end
90       end
91 
92 // eventually replace MTIME logic below with timereg
93 //    timereg tr(PCLK, PRESETn, TIMECLK, memwrite & (entry==16'hBFF8), 1'b0, PWDATA, MTIME, done);
94 
95     always_ff @(posedge PCLK)
96       if (~PRESETn) begin
97         MTIME <= '0;
98       end else if (memwrite & entry == 16'hBFF8) begin
99         // MTIME Counter.  Eventually change this to run off separate clock.  Synchronization then needed
100         for(j=0;j<P.XLEN/8;j++)
101           if(PSTRB[j])
102             MTIME[j*8 +: 8] <= PWDATA[j*8 +: 8];
103       end else MTIME <= MTIME + 1;
104   end else begin:clint // 32-bit
105     always_ff @(posedge PCLK) begin
106       case(entry)
107         16'h0000: PRDATA <= {31'b0, MSIP};
108         16'h4000: PRDATA <= MTIMECMP[31:0];
109         16'h4004: PRDATA <= MTIMECMP[63:32];
110         16'hBFF8: PRDATA <= MTIME[31:0];
111         16'hBFFC: PRDATA <= MTIME[63:32];
112         default:  PRDATA <= '0;
113       endcase
114     end
115     always_ff @(posedge PCLK)
116       if (~PRESETn) begin
117         MSIP <= 1'b0;
118         MTIMECMP <= 64'hFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF; // Spec says MTIMECMP is not reset, but we reset to maximum value to prevent spurious timer interrupts
119       end else if (memwrite) begin
120         if (entry == 16'h0000) MSIP <= PWDATA[0];
121         if (entry == 16'h4000)
122           for(j=0;j<P.XLEN/8;j++)
123             if(PSTRB[j])
124               MTIMECMP[j*8 +: 8] <= PWDATA[j*8 +: 8];
125         if (entry == 16'h4004)
126           for(j=0;j<P.XLEN/8;j++)
127             if(PSTRB[j])
128               MTIMECMP[32 + j*8 +: 8] <= PWDATA[j*8 +: 8];
129         // MTIME Counter.  Eventually change this to run off separate clock.  Synchronization then needed
130       end
131 
132 // eventually replace MTIME logic below with timereg
133 //     timereg tr(PCLK, PRESETn, TIMECLK, memwrite & (entry==16'hBFF8), memwrite & (entry == 16'hBFFC), PWDATA, MTIME, done);
134     always_ff @(posedge PCLK)
135       if (~PRESETn) begin
136         MTIME <= '0;
137         // MTIMECMP is not reset
138       end else if (memwrite & (entry == 16'hBFF8)) begin
139         for(i=0;i<P.XLEN/8;i++)
140           if(PSTRB[i])
141             MTIME[i*8 +: 8] <= PWDATA[i*8 +: 8];
142       end else if (memwrite & (entry == 16'hBFFC)) begin
143         // MTIME Counter.  Eventually change this to run off separate clock.  Synchronization then needed
144         for(i=0;i<P.XLEN/8;i++)
145           if(PSTRB[i])
146             MTIME[32 + i*8 +: 8]<= PWDATA[i*8 +: 8];
147       end else MTIME <= MTIME + 1;
148   end
149 
150   // Software interrupt when MSIP is set
151   assign MSwInt = MSIP;
152   // Timer interrupt when MTIME >= MTIMECMP
153   assign MTimerInt = ({1'b0, MTIME} >= {1'b0, MTIMECMP}); // unsigned comparison
154 
155 endmodule

158 module timeregsync  import cvw::*;  #(parameter cvw_t P) (
159   input  logic              clk, resetn,
160   input  logic              we0, we1,
161   input  logic [P.XLEN-1:0] wd,
162   output logic [63:0]       q);
163 
164   if (P.XLEN==64)
165     always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge resetn)
166       if (~resetn)  q <= '0;
167       else if (we0) q <= wd;
168       else          q <= q + 1;
169   else
170     always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge resetn)
171       if (~resetn)  q <= '0;
172       else if (we0) q[31:0] <= wd;
173       else if (we1) q[63:32] <= wd;
174       else          q <= q + 1;
175 endmodule

178 module timereg  import cvw::*;  #(parameter cvw_t P) (
179   input  logic              PCLK, PRESETn, TIMECLK,
180   input  logic              we0, we1,
181   input  logic [P.XLEN-1:0] PWDATA,
182   output logic [63:0]       MTIME,
183   output logic              done);
184 
185 //  if (P.TIMEBASE_SYNC) begin:timereg // use PCLK for MTIME
186   if (1) begin:timereg // use PCLK for MTIME
187     timregsync timeregsync(.clk(PCLK), .resetn(PRESETn), .we0, .we1, .wd(PWDATA), .q(MTIME));
188     assign done = 1;   // immediately completes
189   end else begin       // use asynchronous TIMECLK
190     // TIME counter runs on TIMECLK but bus interface runs on PCLK
191     // Need to synchronize reads and writes
192     // This is subtle because synchronizing a binary counter on a per-bit basis could give a mix of old and new bits
193     // Instead, we use a Gray coded counter that only changes one bit per cycle
194     // Synchronizing this for a read is safe because we are guaranteed to get either the old or the new value.
195     // Writing to the counter requires a request/acknowledge handshake to ensure the write value is held long enough.
196     // The handshake signals are synchronized in each direction across the interface
197     // There is no back pressure on instructions, so if multiple counter writes occur too close together, the results are unpredictable.
198 
199     logic req, req_sync, ack, we0_stored, we1_stored, ack_stored, resetn_sync;
200     logic [P.XLEN-1:0] wd_stored;
201     logic [63:0] time_int, time_int_gc, time_gc, MTIME_GC;
202 
203     // When a write enable is asserted for a cycle, sample the enables and data and raise a request until it is acknowledged
204     // When the acknowledge falls, the transaction is done and the system is ready for another write.
205     // When adding asynchronous timebase, look at redoing this assuming write enable and data are held rather than pulsed.
206     always_ff @(posedge PCLK or negedge PRESETn)
207       if (~PRESETn)
208         req <= 0; // don't bother resetting wd
209       else begin
210         req        <= we0 | we1 | req & ~ack;
211         we0_stored <= we0;
212         we1_stored <= we1;
213         wd_stored  <= PWDATA;
214         ack_stored <= ack;
215         done       <= ack_stored & ~ack;
216       end
217 
218     // synchronize the reset and request into the TIMECLK domain
219     sync resetsync(TIMECLK, PRESETn, resetn_sync);
220     sync rsync(TIMECLK, req, req_sync);
221     // synchronize the acknowledge back to the PCLK domain to indicate the request was handled and can be lowered
222     sync async(PCLK, req_sync, ack);
223 
224     timeregsync #(P) timeregsync(.clk(TIMECLK), .resetn(resetn_sync), .we0(we0_stored), .we1(we1_stored), .wd(wd_stored), .q(time_int));
225     binarytogray b2g(time_int, time_int_gc);
226     flop gcreg(TIMECLK, time_int_gc, time_gc);
227 
228     sync timesync[63:0](PCLK, time_gc, MTIME_GC);
229     graytobinary g2b(MTIME_GC, MTIME);
230   end
231 endmodule
232 
233 module binarytogray #(parameter N) (
234   input  logic [N-1:0] b,
235   output logic [N-1:0] g);
236 
237   // G[N-1] = B[N-1]; G[i] = B[i] ^ B[i+1] for 0 <= i < N-1
238   // requires single layer of N-1 XOR gates
239   assign g = b ^ {1'b0, b[N-1:1]};
240 endmodule
241 
242 module graytobinary #(parameter N) (
243   input  logic [N-1:0] g,
244   output logic [N-1:0] b);
245 
246   // B[N-1] = G[N-1]; B[i] = G[i] ^ B[i+1] for 0 <= i < N-1
247   // requires rippling through N-1 XOR gates
248     genvar i;
249     assign b[N-1] = g[N-1];
250     for (i=N-2; i >= 0; i--) begin:g2b
251       assign b[i] = g[i] ^ b[i+1];
252     end
253 endmodule

32 module csr import cvw::*;  #(parameter cvw_t P) (
33   input  logic                     clk, reset,
34   input  logic                     FlushM, FlushW,
35   input  logic                     StallE, StallM, StallW,
36   input  logic [31:0]              InstrM,                    // current instruction
37   input  logic [31:0]              InstrOrigM,                // Original compressed or uncompressed instruction in Memory stage for Illegal Instruction MTVAL
38   input  logic [P.XLEN-1:0]        PCM,                       // program counter, next PC going to trap/return logic
39   input  logic [P.XLEN-1:0]        PCSpillM,                  // program counter, next PC going to trap/return logic aligned after an instruction spill
40   input  logic [P.XLEN-1:0]        SrcAM, IEUAdrxTvalM,       // SrcA and memory address from IEU
41   input  logic                     CSRReadM, CSRWriteM,       // read or write CSR
42   input  logic                     TrapM,                     // trap is occurring
43   input  logic                     mretM, sretM,              // return instruction
44   input  logic                     InterruptM,                // interrupt is occurring
45   input  logic                     ExceptionM,                // interrupt is occurring
46   input  logic                     MTimerInt,                 // timer interrupt
47   input  logic                     MExtInt, SExtInt,          // external interrupt (from PLIC)
48   input  logic                     MSwInt,                    // software interrupt
49   input  logic [63:0]              MTIME_CLINT,               // TIME value from CLINT
50   input  logic                     InstrValidM,               // current instruction is valid
51   input  logic                     FRegWriteM,                // writes to floating point registers change STATUS.FS
52   input  logic [4:0]               SetFflagsM,                // Set floating point flag bits in FCSR
53   input  logic [1:0]               NextPrivilegeModeM,        // STATUS bits updated based on next privilege mode
54   input  logic [1:0]               PrivilegeModeW,            // current privilege mode
55   input  logic [3:0]               CauseM,                    // Trap cause
56   input  logic                     SelHPTW,                   // hardware page table walker active, so base endianness on supervisor mode
57   // inputs for performance counters
58   input  logic                     LoadStallD, StoreStallD,
59   input  logic                     ICacheStallF,
60   input  logic                     DCacheStallM,
61   input  logic                     BPDirWrongM,
62   input  logic                     BTAWrongM,
63   input  logic                     RASPredPCWrongM,
64   input  logic                     IClassWrongM,
65   input  logic                     BPWrongM,                  // branch predictor is wrong
66   input  logic [3:0]               IClassM,
67   input  logic                     DCacheMiss,
68   input  logic                     DCacheAccess,
69   input  logic                     ICacheMiss,
70   input  logic                     ICacheAccess,
71   input  logic                     sfencevmaM,
72   input  logic                     InvalidateICacheM,
73   input  logic                     DivBusyE,                  // integer divide busy
74   input  logic                     FDivBusyE,                 // floating point divide busy
75   // outputs from CSRs
76   output logic [1:0]               STATUS_MPP,
77   output logic                     STATUS_SPP, STATUS_TSR, STATUS_TVM,
78   output logic [15:0]              MEDELEG_REGW,
79   output logic [P.XLEN-1:0]        SATP_REGW,
80   output logic [11:0]              MIP_REGW, MIE_REGW, MIDELEG_REGW,
81   output logic                     STATUS_MIE, STATUS_SIE,
82   output logic                     STATUS_MXR, STATUS_SUM, STATUS_MPRV, STATUS_TW,
83   output logic [1:0]               STATUS_FS,
84   output var logic [7:0]           PMPCFG_ARRAY_REGW[P.PMP_ENTRIES-1:0],
85   output var logic [P.PA_BITS-3:0] PMPADDR_ARRAY_REGW[P.PMP_ENTRIES-1:0],
86   output logic [2:0]               FRM_REGW,
87   output logic [3:0]               ENVCFG_CBE,
88   output logic                     ENVCFG_PBMTE,              // Page-based memory type enable
89   output logic                     ENVCFG_ADUE,               // HPTW A/D Update enable
90   // PC logic output from privileged unit to IFU
91   output logic [P.XLEN-1:0]        EPCM,                      // Exception Program counter to IFU PC logic
92   output logic [P.XLEN-1:0]        TrapVectorM,               // Trap vector, to IFU PC logic
93   //
94   output logic [P.XLEN-1:0]        CSRReadValW,               // value read from CSR
95   output logic                     IllegalCSRAccessM,         // Illegal CSR access: CSR doesn't exist or is inaccessible at this privilege level
96   output logic                     BigEndianM                 // memory access is big-endian based on privilege mode and STATUS register endian fields
97 );
98 
99   localparam MIP = 12'h344;
100   localparam SIP = 12'h144;
101 
102   logic [P.XLEN-1:0]       CSRMReadValM, CSRSReadValM, CSRUReadValM, CSRCReadValM;
103   logic [P.XLEN-1:0]       CSRReadValM;
104   logic [P.XLEN-1:0]       CSRSrcM;
105   logic [P.XLEN-1:0]       CSRRWM, CSRRSM, CSRRCM;
106   logic [P.XLEN-1:0]       CSRWriteValM;
107   logic [P.XLEN-1:0]       MSTATUS_REGW, SSTATUS_REGW, MSTATUSH_REGW;
108   logic [P.XLEN-1:0]       STVEC_REGW, MTVEC_REGW;
109   logic [P.XLEN-1:0]       MEPC_REGW, SEPC_REGW;
110   logic [31:0]             MCOUNTINHIBIT_REGW, MCOUNTEREN_REGW, SCOUNTEREN_REGW;
111   logic                    WriteMSTATUSM, WriteMSTATUSHM, WriteSSTATUSM;
112   logic                    CSRMWriteM, CSRSWriteM, CSRUWriteM;
113   logic                    UngatedCSRMWriteM;
114   logic                    WriteFRMM, SetOrWriteFFLAGSM;
115   logic [P.XLEN-1:0]       UnalignedNextEPCM, NextEPCM, NextMtvalM;
116   logic [4:0]              NextCauseM;
117   logic [11:0]             CSRAdrM;
118   logic                    IllegalCSRCAccessM, IllegalCSRMAccessM, IllegalCSRSAccessM, IllegalCSRUAccessM;
119   logic                    InsufficientCSRPrivilegeM;
120   logic                    IllegalCSRMWriteReadonlyM;
121   logic [P.XLEN-1:0]       CSRReadVal2M;
122   logic [11:0]             MIP_REGW_writeable;
123   logic [P.XLEN-1:0]       TVecM,NextFaultMtvalM;
124   logic                    MTrapM, STrapM;
125   logic                    SelMtvecM;
126   logic [P.XLEN-1:0]       TVecAlignedM;
127   logic                    InstrValidNotFlushedM;
128   logic                    STimerInt;
129   logic [63:0]             MENVCFG_REGW;
130   logic [P.XLEN-1:0]       SENVCFG_REGW;
131   logic                    ENVCFG_STCE; // supervisor timer counter enable
132   logic                    ENVCFG_FIOM; // fence implies io (presently not used)
133 
134   // only valid unflushed instructions can access CSRs
135   assign InstrValidNotFlushedM = InstrValidM & ~StallW & ~FlushW;
136 
137   ///////////////////////////////////////////
138   // MTVAL: gets value from PC, Instruction, or load/store address
139   ///////////////////////////////////////////
140 
141   always_comb
142     if (InterruptM)           NextFaultMtvalM = '0;
143     else case (CauseM)
144       12, 1, 3:               NextFaultMtvalM = PCSpillM;  // Instruction page/access faults, breakpoint
145       2:                      NextFaultMtvalM = {{(P.XLEN-32){1'b0}}, InstrOrigM}; // Illegal instruction fault
146       0, 4, 6, 13, 15, 5, 7:  NextFaultMtvalM = IEUAdrxTvalM; // Instruction misaligned, Load/Store Misaligned/page/access faults
147       default:                NextFaultMtvalM = '0; // Ecall, interrupts
148     endcase
149 
150   ///////////////////////////////////////////
151   // Trap Vectoring & Returns; vectored traps must be aligned to 64-byte address boundaries
152   ///////////////////////////////////////////
153 
154   // Select trap vector from STVEC or MTVEC and word-align
155   assign SelMtvecM = (NextPrivilegeModeM == P.M_MODE);
156   mux2 #(P.XLEN) tvecmux(STVEC_REGW, MTVEC_REGW, SelMtvecM, TVecM);
157   assign TVecAlignedM = {TVecM[P.XLEN-1:2], 2'b00};
158 
159   // Support vectored interrupts
160   if(P.VECTORED_INTERRUPTS_SUPPORTED) begin:vec
161     logic VectoredM;
162     logic [P.XLEN-1:0] TVecPlusCauseM;
163     assign VectoredM = InterruptM & (TVecM[1:0] == 2'b01);
164     assign TVecPlusCauseM = {TVecAlignedM[P.XLEN-1:6], CauseM, 2'b00}; // 64-byte alignment allows concatenation rather than addition
165     mux2 #(P.XLEN) trapvecmux(TVecAlignedM, TVecPlusCauseM, VectoredM, TrapVectorM);
166   end else
167     assign TrapVectorM = TVecAlignedM; // unvectored interrupt handler can be at any word-aligned address. This is called Sstvecd
168 
169   // Trap Returns
170   // A trap sets the PC to TrapVector
171   // A return sets the PC to MEPC or SEPC
172   mux2 #(P.XLEN) epcmux(SEPC_REGW, MEPC_REGW, mretM, EPCM);
173 
174   ///////////////////////////////////////////
175   // CSRWriteValM
176   ///////////////////////////////////////////
177 
178   always_comb begin
179     // Choose either rs1 or uimm[4:0] as source
180     CSRSrcM = InstrM[14] ? {{(P.XLEN-5){1'b0}}, InstrM[19:15]} : SrcAM;
181 
182     // CSR set and clear for MIP/SIP should only touch internal state, not interrupt inputs
183     if (CSRAdrM == MIP | CSRAdrM == SIP) CSRReadVal2M = {{(P.XLEN-12){1'b0}}, MIP_REGW_writeable};
184     else                                 CSRReadVal2M = CSRReadValM;
185 
186     // Compute AND/OR modification
187     CSRRWM =   CSRSrcM;
188     CSRRSM =   CSRReadVal2M | CSRSrcM;
189     CSRRCM =   CSRReadVal2M & ~CSRSrcM;
190     case (InstrM[13:12])
191       2'b01:   CSRWriteValM = CSRRWM;
192       2'b10:   CSRWriteValM = CSRRSM;
193       2'b11:   CSRWriteValM = CSRRCM;
194       default: CSRWriteValM = CSRReadValM;
195     endcase
196   end
197 
198   ///////////////////////////////////////////
199   // CSR Write values
200   ///////////////////////////////////////////
201 
202   assign CSRAdrM = InstrM[31:20];
203   assign UnalignedNextEPCM = TrapM ? PCM : CSRWriteValM;
204   assign NextEPCM = P.ZCA_SUPPORTED ? {UnalignedNextEPCM[P.XLEN-1:1], 1'b0} : {UnalignedNextEPCM[P.XLEN-1:2], 2'b00}; // 3.1.15 alignment
205   assign NextCauseM = TrapM ? {InterruptM, CauseM}: {CSRWriteValM[P.XLEN-1], CSRWriteValM[3:0]};
206   assign NextMtvalM = TrapM ? NextFaultMtvalM : CSRWriteValM;
207   assign UngatedCSRMWriteM = CSRWriteM & (PrivilegeModeW == P.M_MODE);
208   assign CSRMWriteM = UngatedCSRMWriteM & InstrValidNotFlushedM;
209   assign CSRSWriteM = CSRWriteM & (|PrivilegeModeW) & InstrValidNotFlushedM;
210   assign CSRUWriteM = CSRWriteM  & InstrValidNotFlushedM;
211   assign MTrapM = TrapM & (NextPrivilegeModeM == P.M_MODE);
212   assign STrapM = TrapM & (NextPrivilegeModeM == P.S_MODE) & P.S_SUPPORTED;
213 
214   ///////////////////////////////////////////
215   // CSRs
216   ///////////////////////////////////////////
217 
218   csri #(P) csri(.clk, .reset,
219     .CSRMWriteM, .CSRSWriteM, .CSRWriteValM, .CSRAdrM,
220     .MExtInt, .SExtInt, .MTimerInt, .STimerInt, .MSwInt,
221     .MIDELEG_REGW, .ENVCFG_STCE, .MIP_REGW, .MIE_REGW, .MIP_REGW_writeable);
222 
223   csrsr #(P) csrsr(.clk, .reset, .StallW,
224     .WriteMSTATUSM, .WriteMSTATUSHM, .WriteSSTATUSM,
225     .TrapM, .FRegWriteM, .NextPrivilegeModeM, .PrivilegeModeW,
226     .mretM, .sretM, .WriteFRMM, .SetOrWriteFFLAGSM, .CSRWriteValM, .SelHPTW,

312   assign InsufficientCSRPrivilegeM = (CSRAdrM[9:8] == 2'b11 & PrivilegeModeW != P.M_MODE) |
